title: 第17章 血书第18章 守护
content_zh:
雨没有停。
天亮了一点，又暗了回去。乌云像一口倒扣的铁锅，把整座山压在下面，雨从云缝里漏出来，不是下，是倒，一盆接一盆地往地上泼。
肖琪躺在那块平坦的石头上，呼吸越来越浅。
云彩蹲在他身边，把布条解开又缠上，缠了三层，血还是从缝隙里渗出来。布条一揭开，伤口像一张咧着的嘴，边缘翻着，血肉模糊，深的地方能看见白森森的骨头茬。
“止不住，“云彩的声音很低，像是在跟自己说。
南宫燕蹲在肖琪另一边，一只手握着他凉掉的手，另一只手按在他胸口上。他的心跳她能感觉到——一下，一下，每一下都比上一下弱一点，间隔长一点，像是一盏灯芯快烧尽的油灯，还在亮，但随时会灭。
“还撑得住吗？“风暴站在旁边，声音哑哑的。
云彩没有说话，只是又缠了一层布条。
布条是从她自己的袖子上撕下来的。刚才已经撕过两次了，两只袖子都撕到了肘弯以上，露出一截细瘦的小臂，上面有几道旧伤疤，横七竖八的，像是被刀划过的。
南宫燕也撕了自己的衣襟。她的衣襟撕了两条，一条缠在肖琪的左臂上，一条攥在手里，随时准备替换。
但血止不住。
换一条布条，浸透。再换一条，又浸透。好像他身体里的血是换不完的，往外淌，不停地淌，把石头底下都染红了一片。雨水冲过来，把血水搅成淡红色的溪流，顺着岩石的缝隙往山下淌，像是这座山也在流血。
肖琪的脸白得不像活人。
嘴唇没有血色，眼窝深深地凹进去，颧骨的轮廓比昨天更分明了。他的眼睛闭着，眉头皱着，像是还在疼，但已经疼不出声了。雨水落在他脸上，他连睫毛都不动一下。
南宫燕把他的手握得更紧了。
“肖琪，“她叫他，声音很轻，“你听到没有？“
他没动。
“肖琪！“
他的眼皮动了一下。
很轻，轻得像是风吹的。

南宫燕俯下身去，把耳朵凑到他嘴边。他的呼吸很浅，浅得像一根快要断掉的线，呼出来的气是凉的，落在她的耳廓上，像一片雪花。
“你听到就动一下手指，“她说。
她等了很久。
久到雨又从石头上淌下一股水，久到闪电在洞口换了一次岗，久到她以为他不会再动了——
他的手指动了一下。
在她的掌心里，很轻，很轻，像是一只蝴蝶落在花瓣上。
南宫燕的眼泪掉下来了。
她咬住嘴唇，把眼泪擦掉，又把手覆上他的额头。烫。不，凉。不，又烫。他的体温在变，像是一团火在风里摇，忽明忽暗，随时都会灭。
“水……“
他的嘴唇动了。
南宫燕俯下身去听，只听见一个字，含含糊糊的，像是从很深很深的水底浮上来的气泡。
“水……给她水……“
南宫燕愣住了。
她把耳朵又凑近了一点，确认自己没有听错。
“水……给她……“
他在说什么？
他在说——给她水。
他以为自己在战场上。他以为她受了伤。他以为她还在昏迷，需要他喂水。
他快死了，他在昏梦里想的第一件事——是她渴不渴。
南宫燕的眼眶忽然热了。

不是那种想哭的热，是一种从身体很深的地方涌上来的热，热到她整个人都在发抖。
她蹲在那里，雨水从她的头发上滴下来，滴在他的手背上，和血混在一起。她看着他的脸，看着他的嘴唇一张一合，说着含混不清的话——
“水……“
她站起来。
风云雷闪四个人都看着她。
content_en:
The rain didn't stop.
It gets brighter and then gets darker again. The dark clouds were like an inverted iron pot, pressing the entire mountain underneath. Rain leaked out from the cracks in the clouds. Instead of falling, it poured, pouring basin after basin onto the ground.
Xiao Qi lay on the flat stone, breathing more and more shallowly.
Yun Cai squatted beside him, unwrapped and wrapped the cloth three times, but blood still seeped out from the gaps. Once the strip of cloth was uncovered, the wound looked like a grinning mouth, with the edges turned over and the flesh and blood blurred, and white bone stubble could be seen in the deep places.
"Can't stop," Yun Cai's voice was very low, as if he was telling himself.
Nangong Yan squatted on the other side of Xiao Qi, holding his cold hand with one hand and pressing his chest with the other. She could feel his heartbeat - one after another, each one a little weaker than the previous one, with a longer interval, like an oil lamp whose wick was about to burn out, still on, but about to go out at any time.
"Can you still hold on?" Storm stood beside him, his voice hoarse.
The clouds did not speak, but were wrapped in another layer of cloth.
The strip of cloth was torn from her own sleeve. It had been torn twice just now. Both sleeves were torn above the elbow bend, revealing a thin forearm with a few old scars on it, as if cut by a knife.
Nangong Yan also tore off her clothes. Two pieces of her clothes were torn, one was wrapped around Xiao Qi's left arm, and the other was held in her hand, ready to be replaced at any time.
But the bleeding wouldn't stop.
Use another strip of cloth and soak it. Change another one and soak it again. It seemed that the blood in his body could not be replaced, and it was flowing out continuously, dyeing the bottom of the stone red. The rain rushed over, turning the blood into a reddish stream, flowing down the mountain along the cracks in the rocks, as if the mountain was also bleeding.
Xiao Qi's face was so pale that he didn't look like a living person.
The lips were bloodless, the eye sockets were deeply sunken, and the contours of the cheekbones were more distinct than yesterday. His eyes were closed and his brows were furrowed, as if he was still in pain, but he could no longer make a sound. The rain fell on his face, and he didn't even move his eyelashes.
Nangong Yan held his hand tighter.
"Xiao Qi," she called him, her voice was very soft, "did you hear that?"
He didn't move.
"Xiao Qi!"
His eyelids moved.
Very light, as light as the wind.
Nangong Yan leaned down and put her ear to his mouth. His breathing was very shallow, as shallow as a thread that was about to be broken. The breath he exhaled was cold and fell on her ears like a snowflake.
"Just move your finger when you hear it," she said.
She waited a long time.
It was so long that the rain dropped another stream of water from the stone, so long that lightning changed positions at the entrance of the cave, so long that she thought he wouldn't move again——
His fingers moved.
In her palm, it was very light, very light, like a butterfly landing on the petals of a flower.
Nangong Yan's tears fell.
She bit her lip, wiped away her tears, and put her hand on his forehead. hot. No, cool. No, it's hot again. His body temperature was changing, like a fire swaying in the wind, flickering in and out, and going out at any moment.
"Water..."
His lips moved.
Nangong Yan leaned down to listen, and only heard one word, vague, like bubbles rising from the bottom of the deep water.
"Water...give her water..."
Nangong Yan was stunned.
She brought her ears closer to make sure she heard correctly.
"Water...give her..."
What is he talking about?
He was saying - give her water.
He thought he was on a battlefield. He thought she was hurt. He thought she was still unconscious and needed water from him.
He was dying, and the first thing he thought about in his sleep was whether she was thirsty.
Nangong Yan's eyes suddenly became hot.
It wasn't the kind of heat that made her want to cry, it was the kind of heat that surged up from deep within her body, so hot that her whole body was trembling.
She squatted there, rainwater dripping from her hair and dripping on the back of his hand, mixing with the blood. She looked at his face and sawOpening and closing his lips, speaking incomprehensible words——
"Water..."
She stood up.
The four of them, Fengyun Leishan, looked at her.
